topic: Does beam polarization diversity (e.g., RHCP) in satellite systems introduce clutter correlation issues in bistatic radar detection?
response: Beam polarization diversity in satellite systems can introduce clutter correlation issues in bistatic radar detection due to the inherent properties of polarized waves. The use of Right-Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP) or other polarization schemes can lead to correlated signals, affecting the accuracy of bistatic range and Doppler estimates.
reference_context: The reference context discusses the viability of satellite communication systems as illuminators for passive maritime surveillance using bistatic radars. It highlights the importance of considering noise, clutter, and signal bandwidth in radar performance analysis.
